What If You Flew to the Edge of the Solar System?

Episode 54 of a daily journey through the universe. ❄️
The Oort Cloud: a giant shell of icy objects that may surround our solar system, possibly reaching a quarter of the way to the nearest star. No one has ever seen it directly. Voyager 1 will need about 300 years to reach it and tens of thousands to cross it.

segments.text: What if you kept flying until you reached the very edge of our solar system? It's made of ice.
Where do long-period comets come from? Some take thousands, even millions of years to orbit the Sun once.
segments.headline: Where comets come from

segments.text: In nineteen fifty, Dutch astronomer Jan Oort proposed an answer: a giant shell of icy objects surrounding the entire solar system.
segments.headline: Jan Oort's idea

segments.text: It may contain trillions of icy bodies.
And it's enormous. It might stretch a quarter of the way, or more, to the nearest star.
segments.headline: Enormous

segments.text: Yet no one has ever seen it. The objects are too small, too dark, and too far away. We know it's there from the comets it sends us.
segments.headline: Never seen

segments.text: Sometimes a passing star or the pull of our galaxy nudges one of these ice balls, and it begins a long fall toward the Sun.
segments.headline: A nudge, and a fall

segments.text: Remember Voyager one from episode nine? It's the farthest spacecraft from Earth.
segments.headline: Voyager 1

segments.text: Even at its speed, it will need about three hundred years to reach the Oort cloud's inner edge.
And maybe thirty thousand years to pass through it.
Next stop: Life on Venus?. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
